sources.PG: Washington Parent Guide to Teen Driving — page numbers

1.topics: Licensing, permits, intermediate rules, DUI thresholds, insurance

3.topics: Right-of-way at every kind of intersection

4.topics: Lane use, turning, steering, parking, backing

5.topics: Speed, space, following time, freeways, night range

6.topics: Adverse conditions, skids, vehicle failures, crash response

7.topics: Sharing the road: trucks, bikes, buses, trains, emergency zones, road rage

questions.prompt: The comeback tour is six months out and you want your instruction permit before it starts. You're enrolled in an approved driver training course. How old must you be to apply for the permit?
questions.explanation: With an approved course you can apply at 15 (1–10 days before class starts). Without one, you wait until 15½.

questions.prompt: You skip driver training, pass the knowledge exam at 15½, and cruise the block with 'Hold Still' on 91.3. When can you take the skills exam and actually get a license?
choices: As soon as you've held the permit 6 months
questions.explanation: No approved course means no license until 18. The permit still lets you practice with a qualified supervisor.

questions.prompt: Your permit is like a limited-run photocard — it expires. How long is a Washington instruction permit valid before it must be renewed?
questions.explanation: One year, renewable for a fee. Your knowledge-exam score itself is good for 2 years.

questions.prompt: Deac won't stamp anything until the practice log is full. For a 16- or 17-year-old, how much supervised practice does Washington require?
choices: 40 hours of day driving plus 10 hours at night
50 hours of day driving plus 10 at night
questions.explanation: 50 total: 40 daytime, 10 nighttime, attested by a parent or guardian.

questions.prompt: HUSH's road manager offers to ride shotgun while you practice on your permit at 16. To legally supervise a driver under 18, that passenger must be…
choices: A licensed driver with 3 or more years of experience
questions.explanation: 3+ years licensed for under-18 practice. Applicants 18 and over need a supervisor with 5+ years.

questions.prompt: You got your intermediate license three weeks ago. All four HUSH members (ages 18–19) want a lift to the Tacoma Dome. How many may ride with you?
choices: All four — it's a short trip
None — no passengers under 20 except immediate family for the first 6 months
questions.explanation: First six months: zero non-family passengers under 20. OT4 takes the bus.

questions.prompt: Eight months into your intermediate license, the maknae wants to bring friends to the fansign. What's the maximum number of non-family passengers under 20 you may carry now?
questions.explanation: Months 6–12 (or until 18): no more than three passengers under 20 who aren't immediate family.

questions.prompt: Lightstick-ocean rehearsal at the Harbor runs until 1:30 a.m., and the Quiet are thickest after dark anyway. During your first year on an intermediate license, when may you drive between 1 and 5 a.m.?
choices: Only with a parent, guardian, or licensed driver who is at least 25
Any time, as long as you carry no passengers
questions.explanation: The night restriction lifts after one year of safe driving; until then you need the 25+ supervisor (agricultural work is the other exception).

questions.prompt: Weverse pings — Sori just went live. With a permit or intermediate license, when may you use your phone while driving?
questions.explanation: Permit and intermediate holders can't use a phone at all while driving, even hands-free, except to report an emergency.

questions.prompt: Jonah squeals his tires through one intersection too many and picks up his second traffic violation on an intermediate license. What happens?
choices: A warning letter goes to his parents
License suspended 6 months or until he turns 18, whichever comes first
questions.explanation: 1st: restrictions stay until 18. 2nd: 6-month suspension (or until 18). 3rd: suspended until 18.

questions.prompt: You turn 18 the day of the encore show. What must you do to remove your intermediate restrictions?
choices: Visit a licensing office for a new card
questions.explanation: Restrictions drop off automatically at 18. You can wait until renewal for an updated card.

questions.prompt: Afterparty at the Fandom Harbor. For a driver under 21, what blood alcohol concentration is treated the same as a DUI?
questions.explanation: Under 21: 0.02% BAC, or any active THC above 0.00 ng. Adults: 0.08% / 5 ng.

questions.prompt: Under Washington's Implied Consent Law, what have you agreed to simply by driving here?
choices: To be tested for alcohol or drugs if an officer suspects impairment
To register as an organ donor
To allow a vehicle search at any stop
questions.explanation: Refusing the test can cost your license for 90 to 730 days, or until 21, whichever is longer.

questions.prompt: Ray wants to know what the Beetle's liability policy has to cover. Washington's minimum liability insurance is…
questions.explanation: $25k one person injured, $50k two or more, $10k property damage — and carry proof in the car.

questions.prompt: HUSH adds a Vancouver, B.C. date. An enhanced driver license gets you across the border by land or sea — but it is NOT valid for…
questions.explanation: Enhanced = REAL ID compliant, good for domestic flights, land/sea crossings, federal buildings. International flights still need a passport.

questions.prompt: Priya's cousin moves from Idaho to Kent with a valid Idaho license. How long do new residents have to get a Washington license?
questions.explanation: 30 days for a license, and 30 days to register the vehicle.

questions.prompt: Skills exam day. Mya and Gracie are in their carriers by the door. Who may be in the vehicle during the exam?
choices: You, the examiner, and one parent
You and the examiner only (service animals and sign language interpreters excepted)
You, the examiner, and pets in carriers
questions.explanation: Two people: you and the examiner. The cats wait.

questions.prompt: You move from Grandma June's to the Spokane Relay. How soon must you update your address in License Express?
questions.explanation: Address changes: 10 days, online. Name changes must be done in an office.

questions.prompt: REAL ID is…
choices: A specific card you order online
A federal law setting ID standards — an enhanced license is one way to meet it
questions.explanation: REAL ID is a law, not a card. Standard licenses don't meet it.

questions.prompt: Album versions come in colors; so do signs. A plain yellow sign is telling you…
choices: A general warning about road conditions ahead
questions.explanation: Yellow = warning of general or unexpected conditions (curves, hills, crossings).

questions.prompt: Orange signs line the road into the Valley where the Authority crews are shoring up a bridge. Orange means…
questions.explanation: Orange = work zones. Slow down even if you see no workers.

questions.prompt: The bright yellow-green sign by the old elementary school — the exact shade of Lumi's lightbar — is warning you about…
questions.explanation: Fluorescent yellow-green is reserved for people on foot and on bikes, especially near schools.

questions.prompt: Priya needs an EV charging station for the radio van. Signs pointing to services — gas, charging, hospitals, rest areas — are…
questions.explanation: Blue = motorist services. Green = directions and distances.

questions.prompt: Coming down toward Vantage you pass a sign for the Gorge Amphitheatre, where HUSH played their last outdoor show before the Quiet came. Signs for recreation, cultural, and historic sites are…
questions.explanation: Brown = public recreation and cultural/historic identification.

questions.prompt: The signal at Central and Titus blinks red on emergency power while a dozen of the Quiet stand on the corner. Treat a flashing red light as…
choices: A stop sign — full stop, then go when it's your turn
A dead signal — go if clear
A stop for cross traffic only
questions.explanation: Flashing red functions exactly like a stop sign.

questions.prompt: A flashing yellow light has the same meaning as…
choices: A yield sign — slow down, proceed when you have the right-of-way
questions.explanation: Flashing yellow: treat the intersection as uncontrolled and yield as needed.

questions.prompt: The grid's been dead two years; the signal ahead is completely dark. What do you do?
choices: Proceed — a dark signal means no control
Treat it as a four-way stop: stop, yield to the vehicle on your right, go when safe
Stop only if you see cross traffic
questions.explanation: Broken signal = four-way stop. Habits outlive the power grid.

questions.prompt: Red light, no 'NO TURN ON RED' sign, plenty of room, and your bias just walked into the shop on the corner. May you turn right?
choices: Yes, after coming to a complete stop and checking for pedestrians
Yes, without stopping if nobody's coming
questions.explanation: Right on red is legal after a full stop unless a sign prohibits it. Your bias on the sidewalk is a pedestrian — yield.

questions.prompt: Red light. You want to turn left onto a one-way street and no sign prohibits it. May you?
choices: Never — left on red is always illegal
Yes, after a complete stop, when there's room to enter traffic safely
Only if the cross street's light is also red
questions.explanation: Washington allows a left turn on red onto a one-way street after a complete stop, absent a sign.

questions.prompt: The light goes solid yellow as you approach. The maknae yells 'floor it!' Out here a hard throttle is also a dinner bell. Legally, you…
choices: May accelerate to clear the intersection
May not exceed the posted limit to enter or clear it — slow down and prepare to stop
Must stop immediately, even if you're already in the intersection
questions.explanation: Yellow means prepare to stop. If you're already inside, continue at the posted speed.

questions.prompt: A red arrow means…
choices: You may not travel in the arrow's direction
questions.explanation: Red arrow: no movement in that direction until it changes.

questions.prompt: A green arrow gives you…
choices: The right-of-way in that direction — no oncoming, crossing, or pedestrian traffic should be moving
Permission to turn only if you yield
A warning the light is changing
questions.explanation: Green arrow = protected turn. Still look; someone may run the red.

questions.prompt: Square sign, a white horizontal bar inside a red circle. It means…
choices: Do Not Enter from this direction
questions.explanation: That's DO NOT ENTER. If you're already past it, the next sign you'll see is WRONG WAY.

questions.prompt: WRONG WAY. Nobody's coming — nobody's ever coming — but the sign is still right. You…
questions.explanation: The sign exists to prevent head-on collisions. Stop and turn around.

questions.prompt: Double solid yellow centerline. Jonah's van is crawling ahead of you. May you pass?
choices: Yes, if the oncoming lane is clear
No — no passing in either direction
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow = no passing for anyone.

questions.prompt: The centerline is solid yellow on your side and dashed on the other. May you pass?
choices: No — you may not pass when the solid line is on your side
Only if the other lane is empty
questions.explanation: Dashed on your side means you may pass when safe. Solid on your side means you may not.

questions.prompt: Two solid white lines run between your lane and the next. You may…
choices: Cross to change lanes if safe
Not cross — double solid white is a barrier
Cross only to enter an HOV lane
questions.explanation: Crossing double solid white lines is illegal.

questions.prompt: The shared center lane has left-turn arrows painted both ways. Your friend wants to use it to shoot past a slow truck for a better fancam angle. That lane is for…
choices: Left turns (and permitted U-turns) only — never passing, and no more than 300 feet of travel
Getting around a stopped school bus
questions.explanation: Center turn lanes are two-way turn pockets; watch for oncoming drivers using the same lane.

questions.prompt: Reversible express lane. The overhead signal shows a steady yellow X. That means…
choices: The lane is about to change direction — move out as soon as it's safe
questions.explanation: Green arrow = usable. Red X = not yours. Steady yellow X = get out.

questions.prompt: A bike lane on Central is separated from your lane by two solid white lines with diagonal cross-hatching between them. The hatched buffer is…
choices: Part of the bike lane — don't enter it unless making a legal turn after checking it's safe
questions.explanation: Buffer = bike lane. Drive in bike lanes only to turn or to cross to a parking spot.

questions.prompt: Bicycle-and-chevron 'sharrow' markings appear in your lane. That tells you…
choices: The lane is shared with bicycles — watch for riders, drive slowly, pass with at least 3 feet
questions.explanation: Sharrows mark a shared lane. Riders position themselves on the marking.

questions.prompt: A green painted bicycle box sits between the stop line and the crosswalk. On red, you…
choices: May not turn right on red; stay behind the white line until the box is clear
Pull into the box for a better view
Treat it like any other intersection
questions.explanation: Bike boxes let cyclists go first on green. No right on red near one.

questions.prompt: The school-zone lights are still flashing on solar power, and there's a bike still chained to the rack. The speed limit is…
questions.explanation: School zones are 20 mph when in effect. Automated cameras can enforce it.

questions.prompt: Automated traffic safety cameras record an image if you…
choices: Run a steady red, fail to stop for a railroad signal, or speed in a school zone
questions.explanation: Those three violations. Tickets are mailed to the registered owner.

questions.prompt: Stop sign, painted stop line, marked crosswalk — and your view of the cross street is blocked by an abandoned bus. Where do you stop, and then what?
choices: Roll through the crosswalk to see
Stop before the stop line; then edge forward slowly until you can see
Stop at the corner past the crosswalk
questions.explanation: Stop at the line first (or crosswalk, or corner if unmarked), then creep forward so crossing drivers see your nose before you see them.

questions.prompt: A freeway ramp meter shows red. You…
choices: Stop at the white line and go when it turns green
Use it only if you're in an HOV
questions.explanation: Ramp meters work like regular signals.

questions.prompt: An 18-inch-wide solid yellow strip with diagonal stripes runs down the middle of the road. It's…
choices: A median — illegal to drive within, over, or across
questions.explanation: Painted medians count the same as concrete ones.

questions.prompt: Your bias from HUSH steps into the crosswalk ahead of you, hood up, headphones in. When may you legally proceed?
choices: As soon as they're out of your lane
Once they've cleared your lane and one additional lane
Once they're on the far sidewalk
Immediately, if you drive slowly around them
questions.explanation: Your lane plus one more. And never swing into oncoming traffic to get around a pedestrian.

questions.prompt: A fan with a guide dog is crossing mid-block. The passenger wants you to tap the horn so they hurry. Per the guide…
choices: Don't honk — it can confuse or frighten the animal; wait until they have completely crossed
questions.explanation: For anyone using a wheelchair, cane, or service animal: wait for the full crossing, no horn. It's also unlawful to interfere with a service animal.

questions.prompt: Four-way stop. You and Deac's truck arrive at exactly the same moment. Who goes first?
questions.explanation: Same time: yield to the right. Otherwise first to stop is first to go.

questions.prompt: Four-way stop. You're turning left; the driver across from you is going straight. You both arrived together. Who goes?
choices: The driver going straight; a left-turner yields to vehicles going straight or turning right
questions.explanation: Left turn yields. Same rule as a two-way stop: turning yields to through traffic.

questions.prompt: Two-way stop. You've stopped and want to turn left; a through vehicle on the cross street is approaching. Who has the right-of-way?
questions.explanation: Turning vehicles yield to vehicles going straight.

questions.prompt: You're leaving the gravel lot behind Bea's sanctuary onto a paved street. No signs. Who yields?
choices: You — a driver entering a paved road from an unpaved road yields
questions.explanation: Uncontrolled intersection rules: yield if you're on unpaved entering paved, or a secondary road entering a state highway.

questions.prompt: At an uncontrolled intersection you must yield in all of these cases EXCEPT…
choices: A vehicle is already in the intersection
You're entering a state highway from a secondary road
You're turning left and a vehicle approaches from the opposite direction
You're going straight and a vehicle on your left arrives after you
questions.explanation: The other three are the guide's yield cases. A later-arriving vehicle on your left yields to you.

questions.prompt: Roundabout ahead. Sixty of the Quiet stand on the center island like an audience. Entering, you must…
choices: Look left and yield to all traffic already in the roundabout, then enter to the right
Look right and yield to entering traffic
questions.explanation: Yield on entry, travel counterclockwise, stay in your lane until you exit.

questions.prompt: Roundabouts are designed for speeds between…
questions.explanation: 15–25 mph. Pick your lane from the sign before you enter.

questions.prompt: Hank's grain truck enters the roundabout ahead of you and drifts across both lanes and up onto the truck apron. That's…
choices: Allowed — large vehicles may use both lanes and the apron; give them room
questions.explanation: Big rigs need two lanes of space in a roundabout. Hang back.

questions.prompt: You're inside a roundabout when an Authority ambulance approaches with lights on. You should…
choices: Continue through to your exit, then pull over to the right
questions.explanation: Never stop in the circle. Exit, then yield like at any intersection.

questions.prompt: Siren behind you — the first one you've heard in a month. Fire trucks, ambulances, and police using lights or sirens always have the right-of-way. You…
choices: Pull to the right side and stop; after it passes, signal and re-enter in the order you were traveling
Pull left to give it the right lane
questions.explanation: Right and stop. Then merge back in turn, not in a scramble.

questions.prompt: A transit bus ahead has signaled and is pulling away from its stop back into your lane. You…
choices: Honk to let it know you're there
questions.explanation: Yield to a transit vehicle signaling to re-enter the roadway in your direction.

questions.prompt: No train has come through Kent in two years. You look both ways anyway, because trains…
choices: Yield to cars at unmarked crossings
Always have the right-of-way and can take up to a mile to stop
Stop for flashing lights like everyone else
Only run on the main track
questions.explanation: Trains always win. They can come from either direction on any track.

questions.prompt: You're on the I-90 on-ramp behind Jonah, matching speed. Who has the right-of-way — you or the vehicles already on the freeway?
choices: The vehicles already on the freeway; you adjust speed to find a gap
questions.explanation: Use the whole ramp, signal, mirrors, and speed up or slow down to fit a safe gap.

questions.prompt: You're on the road that dead-ends into a T-intersection. Who has the right-of-way?
questions.explanation: The through road has priority; your road usually has a yield or stop sign.

questions.prompt: A bicyclist is riding across the intersection inside the crosswalk. Legally they are…
choices: A vehicle — yield as you would to a car
A pedestrian — you must yield in marked and unmarked crosswalks
questions.explanation: Bikes in crosswalks are pedestrians. Bikes in the lane are vehicles.

questions.prompt: Turning left across an oncoming lane. Deac's trick: watch an oncoming car pass a tree and count until it reaches your road. Why?
choices: To see if the driver is impaired
Oncoming traffic has the right-of-way; timing one car tells you how long the next one will take, so you know when you have enough time
To estimate their speed for the report
To make sure they aren't one of the Quiet
questions.explanation: Better too much time than not enough. Approaching traffic has the right-of-way.

questions.prompt: There's no paint at the intersection. Is there a crosswalk?
choices: Yes — every intersection is legally a crosswalk, marked or not
Only if a sign says so
questions.explanation: Unmarked crosswalks carry the same right-of-way as painted ones.

questions.prompt: At a small neighborhood traffic-calming circle, a fire truck goes clockwise around the island — the 'wrong' way. That's…
choices: Allowed — calming circles are built for passenger cars; large vehicles may need to go clockwise. Give them room
A sign the circle is closed
questions.explanation: Same right-of-way rules as any intersection, but expect big vehicles to cut the circle.

questions.prompt: HUSH shoots a music video on an ocean beach in Grays Harbor County, one of the two counties where beach driving is allowed. On the beach, the speed limit is ___ and pedestrians and cyclists have the right-of-way ___.
questions.explanation: The beach is a state highway: 25 mph, hard-packed sand only, people always first.

questions.prompt: An Authority crossing guard in a vest waves you through a red light so a convoy can pass before the Quiet notice. You…
choices: Wait for green — signals always win
Follow the guard; law enforcement, construction workers, and crossing guards can overrule signals
questions.explanation: People authorized to direct traffic override signs and signals.

questions.prompt: The tour van is late for the ferry to the Kitsap Harbor. Cutting into the ferry holding line is…
choices: A traffic offense that can lead to a fine
questions.explanation: Ferry line-cutting is an offense. Bicyclists do get priority loading — that's the exception.

questions.prompt: Turning right from a two-lane street onto a four-lane street. Which lane must you turn into?
choices: The lane closest to the direction you came from (the nearest right lane)
The left lane, then move right
questions.explanation: Nearest legal lane in, nearest legal lane out. Change lanes after the turn if needed.

questions.prompt: Nobody alive is behind you on Central, but you signal anyway. How far before a turn or lane change must you signal?
questions.explanation: At least 100 feet. Then make sure the signal cancels after the turn.

questions.prompt: Two left-turn lanes side by side. You're in the outer one. During the turn you must…
choices: Stay in your own lane all the way through the turn
Turn wide into the far lane
questions.explanation: Multiple turn lanes: hold your lane. Change lanes only after the turn is complete.

questions.prompt: You missed the turn for the pop-up shop where Priya trades photocards. No sign prohibits U-turns. Where is a U-turn NOT allowed?
choices: On a curve or approaching the crest of a hill, where you can't see in all directions
At an intersection with a signal
questions.explanation: U-turns are generally legal in Washington unless posted, but you need clear visibility in every direction.

questions.prompt: Multiple lanes in your direction, light traffic. Which lane should you normally drive in?
choices: The right lane; use the left to pass
The carpool lane if you have a passenger
questions.explanation: Keep right except to pass. Carpool lanes are not passing lanes, and you follow the limit even while passing.

questions.prompt: Traffic's stopped for a dormant cluster in the road. The shoulder is wide open. May you use it to get around?
choices: No — don't drive or pass on the shoulder unless directed by officials or signs
Yes, if your hazards are on
questions.explanation: Shoulders aren't travel lanes.

questions.prompt: You blow past the Issaquah exit. Gracie yells. Can you back up along the shoulder to reach it?
choices: No — it's illegal to back up on a shoulder or freeway; take the next exit
Yes, if nobody is behind you
questions.explanation: Keep moving forward. Backing on a freeway is illegal and dangerous.

questions.prompt: Perfect spot right in front of the fansign venue — next to a fire hydrant. How far from a hydrant must you park?
questions.explanation: 15 feet from a hydrant.

questions.prompt: How far from a stop sign, yield sign, or traffic signal must you park?
questions.explanation: 30 feet. (Railroad crossings: 50. Driveways: 5. Fire station driveway, opposite side: 75.)

questions.prompt: You want to park near the tracks to wait out a passing swarm. The minimum distance from a railroad crossing is…
questions.explanation: 50 feet from a crossing — and never on the tracks.

questions.prompt: Parallel parked on a street with a curb, your tires may be no more than ___ from the curb.
questions.explanation: 12 inches. And never park facing oncoming traffic.

questions.prompt: Parking the Beetle facing DOWNHILL on a Spokane street with a curb. Which way do you turn the wheels?
choices: Toward the curb, so the front tire rests against it
It doesn't matter if the parking brake is set
questions.explanation: Downhill: toward the curb. If the brake fails, the car rolls into the curb, not the road. Always set the parking brake.

questions.prompt: Parking facing UPHILL next to a tall curb. Which way do you turn the wheels?
choices: Away from the curb, so the back of the front tire touches the curb
questions.explanation: Uphill with a tall curb: away from the curb. With a low rounded curb, toward the curb may be safer.

questions.prompt: Parking on a hill on the pass road with no curb at all. Turn the wheels…
choices: Toward the center of the road
Toward the edge of the road, so a rolling car leaves traffic
questions.explanation: No curb: toward the edge, uphill or down.

questions.prompt: You've parked outside the venue and a stream of fans on bikes is rolling past. The 'Dutch Reach' means opening your door with…
choices: The hand farthest from the door, which turns your body to see approaching cyclists
questions.explanation: Far hand forces the shoulder check and slows the door.

questions.prompt: Bea asks you to watch her 11-year-old nephew for five minutes while she loads cat food. Leaving him alone in the parked Beetle is…
choices: Fine if the doors are locked
A crime — a child under 12 may not be left unattended in a parked vehicle (under 16 if the engine is running)
Only a problem in hot weather
questions.explanation: Same for animals at risk from heat, cold, or no water. Law enforcement can break in to remove them.

questions.prompt: The only open space at the Harbor is an EV charging stall. Priya's gas van may park there…
choices: Never — only a vehicle connected to the charger may occupy it
Overnight if the lot is empty
questions.explanation: It's illegal to park in a charging station unless you're plugged in.

questions.prompt: Hands on the wheel like a clock face. For the best control (and clear of the airbag), the guide recommends…
questions.explanation: Hands on the top half, outside the rim. Hand-to-hand steering keeps arms out of the airbag zone.

questions.prompt: Which situation calls for hand-over-hand steering rather than hand-to-hand?
choices: Low-speed turns, parking, an intersection, or recovering from a skid
questions.explanation: Hand-over-hand for sharp, slow, or corrective steering. One hand at 12 only when backing.

questions.prompt: Your 'bias wrecker' is the one you didn't see coming. On the road, that's the blind zone. When you turn your head to check it, you should…
choices: Steer slightly the same way you look
questions.explanation: New drivers drift toward where they look. Head turns, wheel stays.

questions.prompt: You hang Priya's HUSH eungwonbong (lightstick) from the rearview mirror. Per the guide…
choices: Don't — nothing hanging from the mirror or cluttering the windows that blocks your view
questions.explanation: Same rule for the disabled placard: don't hang it while driving.

questions.prompt: A cyclist is ahead on a two-lane road with one lane each way. To pass, you…
choices: Move into the other lane only when there's no oncoming traffic, pass slowly on their left with at least 3 feet, and don't cut back too soon
Cross into oncoming traffic if the bike is slow
questions.explanation: 3 feet minimum from the widest part of your car. Two lanes your way: move over a full lane. Never into oncoming traffic.

questions.prompt: You're about to turn right and a cyclist is just ahead in the bike lane. You should…
choices: Let the cyclist clear the intersection before turning — never pass a bike just before a right turn
Turn from the bike lane behind them
questions.explanation: The 'right hook' is a classic crash. Wait.

questions.prompt: Tuna hasn't fixed the Beetle's turn signals yet. Left arm out the window, bent at the elbow with fingers pointing up means…
questions.explanation: Straight out = left. Bent up = right. Pointing down = stop or slowing.

questions.prompt: Lane closure ahead of the venue exit; traffic crawling. The correct 'zipper merge' is to…
choices: Merge as early as possible to be polite
Use both lanes to the merge point, then alternate one car from each lane
Speed up and cut in at the end
Stop and wait for a wave
questions.explanation: Zipper merging improves flow by about 60% and makes merging predictable.

questions.prompt: The Beetle has ABS. In an emergency stop, it does what?
choices: Keeps the wheels from locking so you can still steer — it does not shorten the stop; expect the pedal to shake
questions.explanation: Press firmly and steer. Practice it once in an empty lot so the shaking doesn't surprise you.

questions.prompt: The guide's braking image — 'a cup of water in your lap you don't want to spill' — is about which two levels you should use almost all the time?
questions.explanation: Four levels: light, medium, firm, emergency. Smooth braking also doesn't surprise the driver behind you.

questions.prompt: The sign says 60; the road is glazed and the Quiet are on both shoulders. You're doing 50 and get a ticket. How?
choices: You can't — you were under the limit
The limit is for ideal conditions; you can be cited for going too fast for conditions even below it
questions.explanation: Posted limits are maximums under ideal conditions. Slower is your responsibility.

questions.prompt: Some highways post a MINIMUM speed. Its purpose is…
choices: So slow vehicles don't become a hazard to others
questions.explanation: You must travel at least that fast when conditions allow.

questions.prompt: You double your speed from 30 to 60 to catch the ending-fairy shot. Your braking distance…
questions.explanation: Doubling speed quadruples braking distance. Doubling vehicle weight (say, a plow and armored doors) doubles it.

questions.prompt: Below 30 mph, the minimum following time behind the vehicle ahead is…
questions.explanation: 2 or more under 30 mph; 4 or more above 30, in congestion, bad weather, or behind a motorcycle, truck, or bus.

questions.prompt: Jonah brakes hard, it's raining, and you're on the freeway behind him. Deac says four seconds, not three. Which of these does NOT call for a 4-second gap?
choices: A dry residential street at 20 mph
questions.explanation: The slow, dry street is the only 2-second case here.

questions.prompt: The Driver Guide's distance rule near other vehicles: leave at least…
choices: Twice the length of your vehicle
Half a car length in traffic
questions.explanation: At least two vehicle lengths, and more when merging so you can plan, communicate, check, execute, evaluate.

questions.prompt: Hank's loaded truck is doing 55 with properly adjusted brakes. How far does it need to come to a complete stop?
questions.explanation: About 450 feet — a football field and a half. Don't cut in front of it.

questions.prompt: You've passed Hank's rig. When is it safe to move back in front of him?
choices: As soon as your rear bumper clears his front bumper
When you can see both of his headlights in your rearview mirror
questions.explanation: Both headlights in the mirror, then merge and keep the flow.

questions.prompt: Night on I-90, nobody for fifty miles, high beams on. The rule that keeps you from 'outdriving your headlights' is to drive at a speed that lets you…
choices: Reach the next town before midnight
Stop within the lit area of your headlights (usually about 400 feet)
questions.explanation: If your stopping distance is longer than your light, you'll hit it before you see it.

questions.prompt: Low beams light about 182 feet. At 50 mph you need roughly 190 feet to stop. What does that tell you?
choices: At 50 on low beams you're already 'driving blind' — slow down or use high beams when no one's oncoming
You should tailgate to borrow their light
questions.explanation: High beams reach ~350 feet. Use them on empty roads; dim within 500 ft of oncoming traffic.

questions.prompt: Dim your high beams when an oncoming vehicle is within ___ and when you're following within ___.
questions.explanation: 500 feet oncoming, 300 feet behind. If someone won't dim theirs, look toward the right edge of the road.

questions.prompt: Which is NOT an effect of excessive speed listed in the guide?
choices: Less time to scan for hazards
questions.explanation: Speed reduces traction and control; it never improves it.

questions.prompt: The guide names three typical causes of collisions. They are too much speed, too little space, and…
questions.explanation: Speed, space, awareness. The Quiet punish the same three.

questions.prompt: Curve ahead on the pass road. The right sequence is…
choices: Slow before the curve, hold a steady speed through it, accelerate gently as you exit
questions.explanation: Sudden braking or throttle in a curve upsets the car's balance — and the tires scream.

questions.prompt: Approaching a curve, the guide suggests positioning the vehicle…
choices: Slightly to the inside of the lane
Slightly to the outside of the lane, for more room and better visibility around it
questions.explanation: Outside on approach improves sight lines; steer smoothly, no jerky inputs.

questions.prompt: The 'count seconds' drill: pick a utility pole you think is ___ ahead, then count until you reach it. Like timing a fanchant, you get better with practice.
questions.explanation: Guess, count, compare. It builds the distance-judgment novice drivers lack.

questions.prompt: In Washington, vehicle crashes are a leading cause of death for which age group?
questions.explanation: Common fatal factors: speed, impairment, distraction, unrestrained occupants, inexperience.

questions.prompt: The guide's hazard routine is Plan, Communicate, Check, Execute, Evaluate. In the Check step, you set position and speed so you can make the change with no more than…
questions.explanation: If it needs firm braking, you planned too late.

questions.prompt: The OODA Loop the guide recommends for on-road problem solving stands for…
questions.explanation: It's a loop because every situation leads to the next.

questions.prompt: Reading a set list on your dash uses your central vision; catching a shape at the roadside while looking ahead uses…
questions.explanation: Central, fringe, peripheral. Higher speeds degrade all three.

questions.prompt: A yellow sign shows a curve arrow with '35 MPH' under it, but the posted limit is 55. The 35 is…
choices: The legal limit in the curve
An advisory speed — adjust for road, weather, and traffic and follow it
questions.explanation: Speed-warning signs recommend a change for a hazard. Deac's '35' on the pass is the same idea.

questions.prompt: In stop-and-go traffic, often the only 'acceleration' you need is…
questions.explanation: Accelerate like you brake: don't spill the cup of water.

questions.prompt: The best way to avoid hydroplaning is to…
choices: Slow down when the road is wet
Drive in the tire tracks of the car ahead
questions.explanation: Water builds under the tires faster at speed.

questions.prompt: The Beetle starts to float on standing water. You…
choices: Ease off the gas, brake gently, keep the wheel steady, look where you want to go
Shift to neutral and turn the wheel
questions.explanation: No sudden inputs. Wait for the tires to grip again.

questions.prompt: The back of the car steps out on packed snow. A skid on snow screams, and every Quiet on the shoulder hears it. Your first moves are…
choices: Slam the brakes and crank the wheel opposite
Take your foot off the accelerator and steer toward the path you want the car to travel, correcting as it regains grip
Accelerate to pull out of it
Shift to neutral and let go of the wheel
questions.explanation: Foot off, eyes and wheel on the target. With ABS keep steady brake pressure; without it, don't stab the pedal.

questions.prompt: First rain after a hot week — the whole Harbor is outside for the comeback livestream. Why are the first minutes of that rain especially slick?
choices: Heat brings oil in the asphalt to the surface; it's slippery until it washes away
questions.explanation: Give it a few minutes, and give yourself more space.

questions.prompt: On a cold wet day, which surface is most likely to have ice when the rest of the road doesn't?
questions.explanation: Bridges freeze first. So do shady spots.

questions.prompt: 'Black ice' is dangerous mainly because…
choices: It's a thin coating that's hard to see, so drivers don't slow for it
questions.explanation: Near or below freezing, assume it's there even if you can't see it.

questions.prompt: Temperatures rise from well below freezing to near freezing. The road becomes…
choices: More slippery — melting ice becomes a wet layer on top of ice
questions.explanation: Wet ice is worse than dry ice.

questions.prompt: Snoqualmie: the sign reads CHAINS REQUIRED. Tuna told you. Mom told you. Deac told you. What does the sign mean?
choices: Chains (or approved traction tires where allowed) must be used past this point
questions.explanation: Use chains or studded/traction tires when required. Sign says chains, sign means chains.

questions.prompt: Snowy roads call for…
choices: A larger following distance and a dramatically reduced speed
questions.explanation: Space and slowness are the only traction you can add for free.

questions.prompt: BANG — a front tire lets go at 55 on I-90, a hundred yards from a dormant cluster. You…
choices: Grip the wheel firmly, keep it straight, ease off the gas, let the car slow itself, then pull off safely
Shift to neutral and stop in the lane
questions.explanation: Don't brake unless gently and necessary. If you can't reach a safe spot to change it, hazards on and call for help.

questions.prompt: Jonah's engine dies at speed. The wheel gets heavy. He should…
choices: Keep a strong grip — it's hard to turn but it turns — brake with steady pressure, and pull off; then try to restart, raise the hood, hazards on
Coast in the lane and wait
Turn the key off and on repeatedly
questions.explanation: No hard braking. Look for an escape path first.

questions.prompt: The accelerator sticks and the car keeps speeding up. First action?
choices: Turn off the engine at speed
Shift to neutral, keep your eyes on the road, pull off when safe, then turn off the engine
questions.explanation: Neutral kills the drive without killing the power steering.

questions.prompt: Your headlights suddenly go out at night. You…
choices: Keep driving by moonlight to the next exit
Turn on hazards, turn signals, or fog lights if you have them, and pull off as soon as possible
questions.explanation: Any light beats no light. Get off the road.

questions.prompt: The Beetle is dead on the shoulder. Emergency flares should be placed…
questions.explanation: Also: hazards and headlights on, hood up or a white cloth on the antenna or mirror, and don't stand in traffic.

questions.prompt: A gust drops a power line across the Beetle's roof on the Vantage bridge. Nothing's burning. You…
choices: Stay inside, turn off the engine, call 911, and keep others at least 35 feet away — assume the line is live
Push the line off with a lightstick
Drive forward to slide out from under it
questions.explanation: Only if a fire starts do you jump clear — feet together, don't touch the car, shuffle 35 feet away.

questions.prompt: An oncoming driver won't dim their high beams. You should…
choices: Look toward the right edge of the road and use it as a steering guide until they pass
questions.explanation: Never stare into the glare. Slow down, add following distance.

questions.prompt: Vex's signature tinted shades look great in the fancam. Wearing tinted or colored lenses to drive at night or on an overcast day is…
choices: A bad idea — they reduce your vision
questions.explanation: No sunglasses or tinted lenses after dark.

questions.prompt: Following an Authority snowplow closely on the pass is risky mainly because…
choices: Plows throw snow up and off the road, creating blizzard-like visibility for anyone too close
questions.explanation: Hang back and let them work.

questions.prompt: Washington law requires headlights on from ___ until ___.
choices: A half hour after sunset / a half hour before sunrise
questions.explanation: Also any time it's rainy, snowy, foggy, or smoky. Daytime running lights don't turn on your taillights.

questions.prompt: After a crash someone is bleeding but conscious. The guide's order is…
choices: Call 911; don't move them unless there's fire or immediate danger; check breathing, then bleeding — pressure, bandage, tourniquet; keep them warm; no drinks
Move them to the shoulder first
Drive them to the hospital yourself
questions.explanation: Nothing to drink, not even water. Cover them against shock.

questions.prompt: Backing out of a tight Harbor lot, you tap a parked van. Nobody's around and you can't find the owner. You must…
choices: Drive away — no damage, no report
Leave a visible note with the date, time, and your contact information
Call the Relay and log it
questions.explanation: Try to find the owner first. Leaving is hit-and-run.

questions.prompt: A law enforcement officer doesn't respond to your crash. You must file a collision report within…
questions.explanation: 4 days, required by state law. Exchange names, licenses, insurance, and photograph damage.

questions.prompt: At a crash scene the guide says don't smoke because…
choices: Fuel may have spilled and fire is a real danger
questions.explanation: Turn off wrecked vehicles, stay out of traffic lanes, use flares or warning devices.

questions.prompt: Which of these is NOT on the guide's emergency-kit list?
choices: Jumper cables and a backup phone charger
questions.explanation: Also: blanket, water, tool kit, spare tire and jack, and a paper list of important phone numbers.

questions.prompt: 'Pink Bug, if I can't see you in my mirror…' Hank's rule from the guide is: if you can't see a large vehicle's mirrors…
choices: The driver can't see you — you're in a blind zone
questions.explanation: Big rigs have 'No-Zones' on every side, largest on the right. Don't linger there.

questions.prompt: Hank signals right, then swings LEFT before turning. Why, and what do you do?
choices: He's lost — pass on the right
Large vehicles may need more than one lane to turn; never pass a truck while it's turning — wait behind
He's letting you by on the inside
questions.explanation: Passing a turning truck is a frequent cause of collisions. The inside of the turn is a trap.

questions.prompt: A tanker in the convoy carries hazardous-materials placards. The guide says…
choices: Avoid driving near it when possible
Pass it quickly on the left
questions.explanation: Give hazmat loads room.

questions.prompt: On a long steep grade, expect large vehicles to…
choices: Travel slowly, usually in the right lane
questions.explanation: Be ready for slow trucks uphill and down.

questions.prompt: A courier on a motorcycle rides the far right edge of a wide lane. Jae suggests there's room to share it. May you move alongside in the same lane?
choices: Yes, if the lane is wide
No — motorcyclists are entitled to the full lane width; never move into the same lane beside one
questions.explanation: Riders shift position within the lane to see, be seen, and avoid debris.

questions.prompt: The motorcycle ahead slows without its brake light coming on. Likely because…
choices: Riders often slow by rolling off the throttle, not braking — allow extra following room
questions.explanation: Also, some bike turn signals don't cancel automatically. Stay alert around them.

questions.prompt: Before a right turn, the guide's look pattern for hidden motorcycles and bikes is…
questions.explanation: 'Looking twice can save a life.' Plus an over-the-shoulder check for the blind zone.

questions.prompt: Bicyclists on the road have…
choices: The same rights, duties, and responsibilities as a vehicle driver
No right to use a full lane
questions.explanation: They may legally use the full lane. Leave at least 3 feet when following or passing.

questions.prompt: You may drive in a bike lane only when…
choices: Turning, or crossing it to park at the curb
questions.explanation: And look for cyclists before you open your door after parking.

questions.prompt: A school bus ahead in your direction flashes red and extends its stop arm. Kids still ride to the Harbor school. You…
choices: Stop and stay stopped until the lights stop flashing and the arm retracts — then keep watching for children
Stop only if kids are visible
Use the center turn lane to get around
questions.explanation: Everyone in your direction stops, including all turn lanes. Fines are doubled for passing a stopped school bus.

questions.prompt: School bus stopped with red lights on the OTHER side of a road. When do you, traveling the opposite direction, NOT have to stop?
choices: When the road has three or more lanes, or the directions are separated by a median or barrier
questions.explanation: On a two-lane road, both directions stop.

questions.prompt: An Authority tow truck sits on the right shoulder with lights flashing — an emergency zone. You must either move over a lane or…
choices: Slow to at least 10 mph below the limit, and never over 50 in the zone
questions.explanation: Over or slow, never nothing. Applies to tow trucks, utility, waste, maintenance, police, fire, ambulance.

questions.prompt: In a work zone you must yield to…
choices: Highway construction personnel, vehicles with flashing yellow lights, and equipment inside the zone
questions.explanation: Fines double when workers are present. Slow down even when you don't see them — narrow lanes and rough pavement are the hazard.

questions.prompt: An orange triangle emblem on the back of a vehicle means…
choices: A slow-moving vehicle designed for 25 mph or less
questions.explanation: Be patient; pass with a full lane where there are two, or at least 3 feet where there's one.

questions.prompt: Railroad lights flash, bells ring, the gate hasn't dropped yet, and the noise is pulling every Quiet on the block toward the crossing. You stop…
choices: On the tracks to see better
Between 15 and 50 feet from the nearest rail, outside the gates — whether the gate is down or not
Just short of the gate arm
You don't; the gate is still up
questions.explanation: Never drive around a gate. Trains can be closer, quieter, and faster than they look.

questions.prompt: The Beetle stalls ON the tracks. You…
choices: Get everyone (cats included) out immediately and away from the tracks, then call the number on the blue-and-white Emergency Notification sign with the crossing ID — or 911
Push the car with the plow
questions.explanation: People first. The ENS sign is how dispatch stops the train.

questions.prompt: Driving near Link light rail, keep at least ___ between you and a train.
questions.explanation: And never stop, park, or leave your car on the tracks.

questions.prompt: Outside the venue: fans with their backs to you, fans under umbrellas, fans filming with headphones in. Per the guide, these people are dangerous because they…
choices: Can't see you or are distracted — you have to see for them
Have the right-of-way only if they look
questions.explanation: Look for people who can't see you, are distracted, or may be confused (tourists, map-readers).

questions.prompt: A sasaeng-type car is tailgating you, flashing lights, weaving. They're loud enough to wake the whole street. As the target of road rage you should…
choices: Take a breath, move out of the way, avoid gestures, and if followed drive to a populated area with open businesses; call 911 if needed
questions.explanation: Distance yourself physically and mentally. Road rage is a criminal offense; aggressive driving is a traffic offense.

questions.prompt: Reporting an aggressive driver to 911, the guide wants you to give…
choices: Location last seen, plate if known, direction of travel, road, vehicle colors, weapons if any, what happened, and whether you were a victim or witness
questions.explanation: Report in-progress incidents immediately.

questions.prompt: Jonah wants to race a courier van 'for the fancam.' Street racing penalties can include…
choices: Fines, jail, and vehicle impound — for drivers and anyone who instigates or assists
Nothing if no one is hurt
questions.explanation: Racing and unauthorized street demonstrations are among the ways you lose your license.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a listed sign that YOU may be experiencing road rage?
choices: Speeding up to beat a light, using the horn excessively, or braking to stop someone from following too closely
questions.explanation: Allow plenty of time, create space margins, and show grace.

questions.prompt: When following a large vehicle, adjust your following distance so that…
choices: You have a wide view of the roadway ahead
questions.explanation: You can't react to what the truck is hiding.

questions.prompt: Weverse buzzes at a red light — a new HUSH teaser. Holding your phone to look is…
choices: Illegal for every driver — you can't hold any electronic device while driving; hands-free is permitted
questions.explanation: Applies to phones, tablets, gaming devices. Fines after a first violation can double.

questions.prompt: You want the fanchant in your ears without waking the block. Driving with earbuds or noise-canceling headphones in both ears is…
choices: Against the law; one hands-free earpiece in one ear is allowed if it complies with the WAC
questions.explanation: Horns, sirens, and screeching tires are information. Keep an ear open.

questions.prompt: Ellensburg to Vantage, midnight, and you can't remember the last few miles. The guide says…
choices: Pull off the road and take a 20-minute nap
Open the window and push on
questions.explanation: Fatigue is quiet. It gets you before they do.

questions.prompt: On a long trip, plan a stop about every…
questions.explanation: Walk, fresh air, water. Most people need 7–9 hours of sleep to stay alert.

questions.prompt: Which is NOT a listed sign of driver fatigue?
choices: Hitting rumble strips or drifting from your lane
questions.explanation: Frequent mirror checks are a good habit, not a warning sign.

questions.prompt: The most common impairing substance in impaired-driving crashes is ___; the most common impairment in FATAL crashes is ___.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol, cannabis, and other drugs multiplies effects.

questions.prompt: A 22-year-old crew member legally uses a cannabis edible at the afterparty, then wants to drive the van. The guide's position on cannabis and driving is…
choices: There is no safe amount — driving after any cannabis use is illegal at every age
questions.explanation: Legal to possess at 21+, never legal to drive on.

questions.prompt: Your new allergy medicine says 'may cause drowsiness; do not operate heavy machinery.' That warning…
choices: Includes driving — don't drive on a new prescription or higher dose until you know how it affects you
questions.explanation: Legal doesn't mean safe. Impaired driving is criminal regardless of the drug's source.

questions.prompt: You've been drinking, so you sit in the parked car with the keys to 'sleep it off' in the driver's seat. DUI law…
choices: Doesn't apply — the car isn't moving
Can still apply, because being in physical control of the vehicle counts
Applies only if the engine is running
questions.explanation: If you can take control of the engine or operation, you're in physical control.

questions.prompt: The band's manager has an open bottle from the wrap party. Where may open alcohol or cannabis be transported?
choices: Only in the trunk or truck bed — not in any compartment the driver can reach
Anywhere if the driver is sober
questions.explanation: Open-container violations apply to passengers too.

questions.prompt: Gracie escapes her carrier and climbs into your lap while you drive. The guide classifies a loose animal as…
choices: A potential distraction; it's illegal to do anything that takes your focus off driving
Only a problem at highway speed
A passenger, subject to seat-belt law
questions.explanation: Animals outside the cab (truck beds) need a harness or enclosure; transporting them unsafely is a misdemeanor.

questions.prompt: Replaying the comeback stage in your head while the road goes by is which type of distraction?
questions.explanation: Daydreaming, worrying, and strong emotions are mental distractions. Billboards are outside; phones are inside; fatigue is physical.

questions.prompt: Talking to the maknae while steering and watching mirrors is which kind of attention?
questions.explanation: Divided = several things at once. The guide's advice: resist multitasking behind the wheel and limit passengers.

questions.prompt: Before leaving the Harbor lot you're wound up about a photocard trade gone wrong. A calming technique the guide suggests for a parked car is…
choices: Breathe in through your nose and exhale like you're cooling hot soup, or count backward from 100 by threes
questions.explanation: Anxious drivers get heavy on the accelerator. Notice the feeling, then drive.

questions.prompt: Bea's 12-year-old nephew calls shotgun. Children under ___ should never ride in the front seat because of airbags.
questions.explanation: Airbags can seriously injure or kill children. Back seat until 13.

questions.prompt: The shoulder belt is annoying so you tuck it under your arm. That's…
choices: Never — the belt goes across the middle of the chest and shoulder, lap belt snug on the hips, never behind the back or under the arm
Fine if the lap belt is tight
questions.explanation: Buckling correctly is the single most effective thing you can do.

questions.prompt: A 6-year-old who is 4 feet tall rides in…
choices: A booster or car seat — required until the belt fits properly, typically 4'9" (ages 8–12)
questions.explanation: Rear-facing to 2; harness 2–4; booster from 4 until the belt fits.

questions.prompt: Adjusting the driver's seat: your chest should be at least ___ from the steering wheel, and the headrest even with your ___.
questions.explanation: 10 inches leaves room for the airbag; headrest at ear height protects against whiplash.

questions.prompt: The guide's 'before you go' checklist ends with checking in with yourself. Which question is on it?
choices: Are your emotions under control so you can make wise choices behind the wheel?
questions.explanation: Also: healthy and clear-headed? Ready to focus? If not, let someone else drive.

questions.prompt: The van's roof is stacked with unsecured lightstick crates for the Harbor show. Driving with an unsecured load is…
choices: Illegal and dangerous — tie everything down; you and your passengers are responsible for items that fall or blow out
questions.explanation: Litter and debris cause crashes; Washington's littering fines are severe.

questions.prompt: You idle the Beetle in the closed Valley garage to stay warm while sorting photocards. The guide warns that…
choices: Idling in a garage can release lethal carbon monoxide
It's fine with the door cracked
questions.explanation: Turn the engine off when parked for a while.

questions.prompt: According to the Parent Guide, why are extra teen passengers such a risk for a new driver — even quiet ones?
choices: Teen crash rates rise with each teen passenger; they distract and can encourage speeding or showing off
questions.explanation: It's why the intermediate license limits passengers under 20 for the first year.

questions.prompt: The Parent Guide notes the brain region that inhibits risky behavior isn't fully developed until about age…
questions.explanation: Reaction time and coordination peak in the teens; judgment lags. Practice and rules bridge the gap.

questions.prompt: Deac's end-of-run debrief matches the guide's self-evaluation. Which question is on it?
choices: Did anything surprise me, and did I surprise anyone?
How many photocards did you find?
questions.explanation: Also: Was my driving legal, proficient, and smooth? What do I change next time?
